pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/components/report/dimensionShareParity.test.ts:53 The parity gate computes dimensionShares and passes the share into dimFacts/DimensionDetail itself. No test drives DimensionExplorer, so if the production call site (DimensionExplorer.tsx:37) dropped the share, dimFacts would fall back to the raw lens weight (dimensionExplorerDerive.ts:45) and the gate that 'keeps either side from re-forking' would stay green.

techniques.evidence: src/components/report/dimensionShareParity.test.ts:53 The rule 'when a condition is extracted into a shared predicate, assert its adoption' is not met: the suite drives the predicate and supplies its output at the call site, so the adoption in DimensionExplorer is never reached. Reach probe: remove shares.get(d.id) at DimensionExplorer.tsx:37 and nothing in the suite fails.
src/components/report/DimensionExplorer.tsx:36 Production does take this composition, so this is not a path that only the test builds. The defect is the unpinned adoption recorded above.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/app/_dev-inspector/devLocate.test.ts:104 The guard only checks that each declared root exists (declared to disk), never that each shared root on disk is declared. src/components/kit/ exists and AGENTS.md names it as a shared root, yet it is absent from LIBRARY_ROOTS (devLocate.ts:57-62), and the guard named 'tracks the real repo layout' is green.

techniques.evidence: src/app/_dev-inspector/devLocate.test.ts:104 The describe name claims more than the test checks. Reach probe for that claim: add a shared root without listing it. That is the current tree (src/components/kit/), and the suite is green. Elsewhere in this context, fleet-seed.test.ts:45 does it right (it raised the count above 144 so the disambiguation branch actually runs).
src/app/api/dev/seed-history/route.test.ts:27 Streaming order is proved with a barrier: the first NDJSON line must arrive while repo two is held. There is no wall-clock bound.

src/app/api/dev/seed-fleet/route.ts:42 Seed data goes through the product's own write path rather than raw inserts, which is what seeded-data honesty asks for. fleet-seed.test also pins that real stars and visibility are carried through.
src/lib/dev/empty-gate.test.ts:28 The gate takes its env explicitly, so the test inherits nothing from the developer's process environment.

src/app/_dev-inspector/devLocate.test.ts:63 This emits a command line for the VS Code CLI, which is not available in the unit lane. The test uses the fallback the technique allows: a whole-line, anchored string pin rather than a substring.
